latest_release.name: v0.11.0
latest_release.body:
A big one for a small library 🎬

## ✨ New
- **`animations`**: turn single animations off and keep the defaults for the rest, e.g. `autoAnimate(el, { animations: { remain: false } })` next to drag-and-drop libraries that already move items. (#153, #255)
- **`onAnimationEnd(el, action)`**: a callback when each `add` / `remove` / `remain` animation finishes (not on cancel). For `remove` the element has already left the DOM. (#37, #255)
- **`stagger`**: items added together cascade in, e.g. `autoAnimate(list, { stagger: 60 })`. Only entry animations are delayed; waiting items stay hidden. (#44, #256)
- **Svelte 5 attachment**: `import { autoAnimate } from '@formkit/auto-animate/svelte'`, then `<ul {@attach autoAnimate}>` or `{@attach autoAnimate({ duration })}` (options stay reactive). `use:autoAnimate` still works. (#235, #257)

## 🐞 Fixes
- **Table rows**: a removed `<tr>` keeps its cell layout while it fades out. No more collapsed cells or rows floating outside the table; handles `border-spacing`/`border-collapse`, header rows and scaled tables in Chrome, Firefox and Safari. (#7, #260)

## 📚 Docs
- Tips for scrollbar flicker in `overflow: auto` containers (#16) and for stretching flex items (`flex: 1`) (#70).

All new options default to off/unchanged, so existing behavior is the same.

AutoAnimate is a zero-config, drop-in animation utility that adds smooth transitions to your web app. You can use it with Vue, React, Solid or any other JavaScript application. With one line of code, you can improve your interfaces, for example: ## Installation Install using your package manager of choice. ```bash # yarn yarn add @formkit/auto-animate # npm npm install @formkit/auto-animate # pnpm pnpm add @formkit/auto-animate ``` Boom! Done.
